The closing commit rewrote that acceptance to say the fix is handed to M20 row 20. The reason holds: no trace was kept and 50 loaded reruns passed. The instrumentation is the only step possible, and the M20 row and roadmap Deferred row exist. findings.summary: M19.59 now runs the installed-witness probe as three Node test processes at once, each with its own owned browser. The probe used to run serially. Concurrent browser launches on a loaded runner are what caused the macOS cli-mcp witness transport timeout behind M19.33 (ci 43658352359). m19-complete's ci-evidence leg still needs that macOS job green in 2 later runs, and it has 0 today. The change can make that leg harder to close, though it cannot make it falsely green.

dispositions.note: Ratify M19.29's deferral as a checkpoint hand-off in the cp8 record commit. Amend M20.md row 20 to also cite 'M19 cp8 F1', and the roadmap Deferred row for the first-screen stall to cite 'cp8 F1' (it already names M19 and M20). Annotate docs/milestones/M19.md 'Handed off from M18' row 23 so its fix clause reads as handed to M20 row 20 (cp8 F1), and the plan and backlog agree.

The ci-evidence leg needs two green macOS cli-mcp runs, so a regression stays red and visible, never falsely green. If a macOS cli-mcp run after 4ec49e2 fails with a witness transport or launch timeout, the first response is to run the probe parts serially on macOS (or all of them serially). No timeout is raised, and the failure counts as an ADR-0176 attempt on a Fixes-ci row.

The item is listed in plan row 21 (handed from M18), and cutting it is a human scope decision. It does not weaken main's push runs or the nightly, which keep every engine. The driver may ask the human to descope M19.57 rather than spend a commit on it. Otherwise it lands as specified with its ci.yml harness case.

planDelta: 61 rows against 31 planned (1.97x), up from 55 at cp7. All six new rows are M19.28's test-speed split (M19.56 to M19.61), which that row's acceptance allowed and plan row 21 listed item by item. None is new scope.
